messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Kannada, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Kannada line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
ನಾನು ಅವನನ್ನು ಮಹಾ ಮರುಭೂಮಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ನೋಡಿದಾಗ, ನಾನು ಅವನಿಗೆ ನನ್ನ ಮೇಲೆ ಕರುಣೆ ಮಾಡು ಎಂದು ಕೂಗಿದೆ, ನೀನು ಯಾವರೂ ಆಗಿದ್ದರೂ ನೆರಳು ಆಗಿರಲಿ ಅಥವಾ ನಿಜವಾದ ಮಾನವ ಆಗಿರಲಿ!

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table (Step 3)**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation (Eng.) | Status | |-------------|----------------------|----------------------|--------------------------|--------| | Quando | temporal “when” (introduces clause) | ನೋಡಿದಾಗ | “when (I) saw” | OK | | vidi | “saw” (past) | ನೋಡಿದ | “saw” | OK | | costui | demonstrative “him” | ಅವನನ್ನು | “him (ACC)” | OK | | nel | preposition “in” + article “the” | ಮರುಭೂಮಿಯಲ್ಲಿ | “in the desert” | OK | | gran | adjective “great” | ಮಹಾ | “great” | OK | | diserto | noun “desert” | ಮರುಭೂಮಿಯಲ್ಲಿ | “desert (LOC)” | OK | | Miserere | imperative “have pity” | ಕರುಣೆ ಮಾಡು | “have pity” | OK | | di | preposition “on” (target of pity) | ಮೇಲೆ | “on” | OK | | me | pronoun “me” | ನನ್ನ | “my” (object) | OK | | gridai | “I cried / shouted” (past) | ಕೂಗಿದೆ | “cried / shouted” | OK | | a | preposition “to” (dative) | — | (absorbed in “ಅವನಿಗೆ”) | UNNECESSARY | | lui | pronoun “him” (dative) | ಅವನಿಗೆ | “to him” | OK | | qual | relative “whatever” | ಯಾವರೂ | “whatever” | OK | | che | relative particle (introduces clause) | — | (no lexical equivalent) | UNNECESSARY | | tu | pronoun “you” (2nd sg) | ನೀನು | “you” | OK | | sii | subjunctive “be” | ಆಗಿದ್ದರೂ | “be (if/though)” | OK | | od (1st) | disjunction “or” | ಅಥವಾ | “or” | OK | | ombra | noun “shade” | ನೆರಳು | “shade” | OK | | od (2nd) | disjunction “or” | — | (single “ಅಥವಾ” already covers both) | UNNECESSARY | | omo | noun “man” | ಮಾನವ | “man / human” | OK | | certo | adjective “certain / real” | ನಿಜವಾದ | “real / certain” | OK |
---
### Items Requiring Attention
- **UNNECESSARY**: - **a** – the dative preposition is merged into the Kannada dative pronoun “ಅವನಿಗೆ”. - **che** – relative particle has no standalone word in Kannada. - **od (2nd)** – only one “ಅಥವಾ” is needed to link the two alternatives; the second “od” is therefore redundant.
All other source tokens are represented correctly (OK) with appropriate grammatical agreement in the Kannada translation.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Kannada script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Kannada text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
